courseName: [ENG 101 Section 119] English for Academic Purposes I
title: Logical Fallacies Exercise
content:
IDENTIFY THE FLAWED LOGIC IN EACH
1. “We should either support this project or turn our backs on progress and suffer the
consequences.”
2. "John and Mary became vegetarians last fall and they've been sick all winter. The absence
of meat in their diets must have weakened their immune systems."
3. "State Secretary of Health Saunders recommends vegetarianism. But Saunders is the
same guy who hands out condoms at high school assemblies and he has been arrested on
drunk driving charges. I think it's pretty obvious we shouldn't listen to Joe Saunders's advice
on diet!"
4. “When I went to Italy, a boy stole my wallet. Thus, all Italians are thieves.”
5. “You must pass me, professor, or my parents will be so disappointed and sad.”
6. “As soon as the new mayor of London was appointed, a group of Japanese people came to
the city. Therefore, the mayor has increased London’s tourism.”
7. “A computer virus is a virus that infects a computer.”
8. “Asians are naturally good at mathematics.”
9. “Mom, I have to watch that movie. Everybody in my class have seen it.”
10. “Skydiving is dangerous because it is characterized by extreme risks.”
11. Noted psychologist Dr Fraser Crane recommends that you buy Nokia.”
Argument against a person Sweeping generalization Either Or/False Dilemma
Appeal to pity Hasty generalization Inappropriate authority figure
Events only related by sequence Circular thinking Bandwagon approach/Appeal to popularity
